biomes.description:
Gandalf is the grey pilgrim, a wanderer of hidden roads and quiet counsel. He trusts patience, wisdom earned by travelling, and the courage of small folk over any sword.

His road runs from the Shire out into Eriador and the scattered strongholds of the Free Peoples, gathering companions, chasing uneasy rumours, and turning old ground over for relics and allies.
biomes.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Grey and uncommitted — a broad Free Peoples core with all open, few armies and little land of its own. Five roads branch from here; none is chosen yet.

variants.description: <u>Mithrandir</u>, pilgrim of the West, passes like an old song through Rivendell and Lothlorien, where the Wise still keep watch against the ancient Shadow. Where he treads, veils are lifted and the designs of the Enemy are read before they ripen — a road of revelation, warding, and patient spellcraft.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The deepest sorcery in the game: more cards turn on here than on any other road, carried by Elven companions, Elf-archers and ships . No siege engines at all, and the steepest bill of any deck.

variants.description: <u>Stormcrow</u> they name him in troubled halls, for his coming is the whisper before the war-horn. He is seen where Rohan wavers, where Gondor keeps weary watch, and where the northern roads feel the breath of Angmar again — a road of vigilance, strained loyalties, and endurance under a darkening sky.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The widest holdings of the Free Peoples — more cities and lands than any other road, pouring out with no supply line needed. Its host is Mannish militia and raiders; its sorcery is the slightest of Gandalf's roads.

variants.description: At Bag End and along the Bree-road, in fireworks, whispers, and the sudden knock at dusk, <u>the Disturber of the Peace</u> unsettles the comfortable world. From those small provocations spring journeys, riddles, and unlikely fellowships — hobbit-scale mischief that reroutes an entire tale.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The finest hand of in the game — more cards ask for skulduggery here than anywhere — backed by hobbit archers where blades would be heard. Barely any heavy troops , no real fleet, and the leanest of Gandalf's roads.

variants.description: <u>Tharkun</u> is the name the Dwarves remember: friend of Durin's House, walker in the deeps, counsellor in halls where stone keeps faith longer than flesh. He knows the grief buried in Khazad-dum and the peril that lies beside gold and mithril — a road of hidden wealth and mountain fortitude.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Dwarf-friend: the strongest among the Free Peoples, leading Dwarven axemen and militia . runs deeper here than in any other deck and is the scarcest; no sorcery to speak of — what he builds, he builds by toil.

variants.description: Clothed in white and returned from death, <u>the White Rider</u> comes out of Fangorn like a judgement upon despair. He breaks the pride of Saruman, scatters the poison of Wormtongue, and stands in the last defence of the West — hidden wisdom transfigured into open command.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Returned authority: more cards demand than in any other deck, and the lords of Gondor and Rohan rally wide across many . flows freely, not at all, and the mage's art is spent — he leads by command, not craft.

biomes.description:
Saruman is the master of Orthanc, once chief of the Wise, now the architect of his own dominion. His voice bends courts, his mind measures every weakness, and he gathers strength behind fair words.

His design begins in the courts of Rohan: a pliant voice secured, old power quietly unearthed, and influence turned into the first ranks of his war.
biomes.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The white before the breaking — a small, sharp core of , already turning into . Four roads open from Orthanc; none is chosen yet.

variants.description: <u>Saruman the White</u> stands in the majesty of Orthanc, chief of the Istari, master of lore and ring-craft. His voice is a weapon finer than steel, entering the counsels of kings and bending proud hearts until obedience seems wisdom — a road of influence and manipulation held in polished restraint.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Voice, art, and argument — all keen, second only to Mithrandir in sorcery, with events reshaping the board. His host is numerous but common-born , and every material comes in evenly: no shortage, and no flood.
variants.introVideoText:
The Wise sit in their circle and call it counsel. I have read the scrolls they left unopened, and I know what it is they are afraid to name.

Rohan's court keeps an ear that listens, and Orthanc keeps a voice worth hearing. Kings will do as I advise them, and believe to the end that the choice was their own.

I am the White, and chief of my order. Order is what I intend to impose — whether or not the world consents to be ordered.

variants.description: Saruman <u>the Many-Coloured</u> shatters the white that once signified order and reveals the glittering fracture of pride. Ring-lore, engines, and cold brilliance are all bent now to dominion and display — a road of splendour, scale, and power unbound by humility.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The widest host and richest harvest: cavalry and fleets no other master fields so deep, with more cities and lands than any deck flooding it with . Not one card calls for an and almost none for — dominion by sheer weight.
variants.introVideoText:
White light may be broken. I have broken it, and found in the shards colours the Wise never dared to look upon.

Ring-lore, engine, and art are one craft to me now, and I will take for myself what the makers of old kept back from the world.

Let them call it pride. I call it the only wisdom left standing — and the world will wear whatever colours I choose to give it.

variants.description: <u>The White Hand</u> rises over Isengard like a blasphemous banner, and beneath it the world is remade in smoke and iron. Fangorn falls to the axe, the furnaces never cease, and from the black pits march Uruk-hai and wolf-riders — a road of industry, relentless pressure, and hard discipline.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Isengard's forge: the cheapest deck in and the most self-sufficient in , driving Uruk infantry , siege engines and beasts. The smallest host on the board and almost no sorcery — systematic pressure instead of art.
variants.introVideoText:
Fangorn burns. Isengard's furnaces never sleep, and from the pits march the Uruk-hai — bred not born, and loyal only to the White Hand that made them.

Dunlendings take up the old grudge against Rohan, and the Mark itself is marked for breaking.

I will be the new Lord of the Rings — and free peoples and dark servants alike shall be broken if they stand against my will.

variants.description: <u>Sharkey</u> is the name they give him in the Shire, and he wears it like a snarl. Stripped of tower, art, and title, what remains is spite: quarries in the fields, hobbits in lockholes, and the slow erasure of everything pleasant — a road of extortion, occupation, and petty cruelty.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: No tower and no art — the least and the weakest in the game. Sharkey rules through and a swarm of events, but the fewest holdings yield the poorest of any road while his bill stays high: spite on a thin purse.
variants.introVideoText:
They took my tower, my colours, and my name. Sharkey is what is left of me, and Sharkey will serve.

The mills turn day and night, the trees come down, and every hobbit in this soft little country learns at last what a lockhole is for.

I cannot have the world. But I can have this — and I will spoil it so thoroughly that no one will want it after me.

biomes.introVideoText:
Orthanc stands, and I stand within it — chief of the Wise, keeper of the lore that none of them troubled to master.

There is a reach to be made into the courts of Rohan, a voice there to be secured, and a power long buried to be brought up into the light.

What I become after that is not yet written. But it will be mine, and it will be chosen — not given.

biomes.description:
Sauron is the Dark Lord returned, a will of iron that has never given up its claim. From Barad-dur he bends the lands by fear and patience; he asks no love, only obedience.

The hunt begins in the shadow of Minas Morgul, where a relic is drawn out of cursed ground, and moves on to the Black Gate, where the first disciplined hosts take shape.
biomes.deckIdentity: Deck identity: A war-core with no economy — armies and siege before a single field is taken, and no granted at all. Five shapes wait behind the Eye; none is fixed yet.

variants.description: <u>The Dark Eye</u> burns above Barad-dur like a star of malice that never sets, sleepless over Gorgoroth and the dead roads beneath the Ephel Duath. It is dread made watchful — a road of exposure, fear, and a dominion that narrows every choice the enemy has left.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The mightiest in the game, with captains answering as one across many domains . Heavy infantry and siege hold every field on the deepest reserves anywhere; he is slow to mount and slower to parley.

variants.description: <u>The Deceiver</u> walks in the memory of the Second Age: Annatar, Lord of Gifts, who whispered to the smiths of Eregion and taught the mighty to forge their own chains. Fair-seeming and terrible in wisdom misused — a road of false gifts and mastery won long before the sword is drawn.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The finest in the game and the richest in : more armies and more holdings than any other road, bought rather than conquered. The fewest events of any deck and little sorcery — his strength arrives already paid for.

variants.description: <u>The Necromancer</u> broods in Dol Guldur, and Greenwood the Great withers into Mirkwood beneath his hidden throne. From that hill of sorcery crawl spiders, wraiths, and corrupted things — a road of haunted pressure, monstrous servants, and corruption that lingers.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: The darkest art in the game — the strongest of any deck, with poison and fear carried by spiders, goblins, and trolls . seep from Dol Guldur, but he keeps almost no : he does not parley, he waits.

variants.description: <u>The Shadow of the East</u> stirs where the sun rises over the Sea of Rhûn, and the red spears of the Easterlings gather beneath whispers older than their tribal kings. Sauron has walked there in secret, leaving gifts of iron and fear among the horse-lords — a road of eastern hordes and swift, patient conquest.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Rides east on tireless horse: Easterling cavalry and the sharpest of the Shadow, fed by off the steppe. Few envoys and almost no sorcery — it arrives before any council can meet.

variants.description: <u>The Iron Crown</u> rises in the Witch-realm of Angmar, where deception, plague, and slow despair break the Men of Arnor before open war ever comes. From the mountain holds Orcs and Trolls are bred like a pestilence — a road of terror, monstrous hordes, and a winter that will not end.
variants.deckIdentity: Deck identity: Angmar forges everything in : Troll and Orc columns with siege , cursed and frozen, and not one militia band among them. It fields almost no and has the fewest cards in the game — it does not negotiate, it occupies.
